what: woff2/convert, n=5, on a quiet host: the run that was void on the Mac.
host: Ubuntu 22.04 aarch64 guest, 8 vCPU, load ~1. Every record carries machine_was_busy: false. Same benchmark image as every other run in this repository, transferred rather than rebuilt, so the toolchain is identical.
VERDICT: NOT SIGNIFICANT. p = 1.0 -- the two samples interleave perfectly. There is no measurable difference between the generated harness and the library's own on this case, and the 1.18x median is noise.
why_this_case_cannot_measure_anything: seeds: 0, corpus_files_at_start: 0. woff2 runs with NO seed corpus on either side, so each campaign is a random walk from nothing. The spreads -- 23.98 and 30.87 points -- are an order of magnitude larger than the difference being looked for.
what_a_single_sample_would_have_said: Run 3 alone: 1.49x, 'we beat the hand-written harness by half again'. Run 2 alone: 0.31x, 'we lose by a factor of three'. Same two harnesses, same machine, one hour apart.
the_earlier_diagnosis_was_incomplete: The machine-load section of REPLICATION.md blamed woff2's spread on other work sharing the host. That was a contributing factor, not the cause: the spread is just as large with nothing else running.
what_this_costs_the_paper: woff2 was the second of two C++ head-to-head cases. It cannot carry a ratio. pugixml -- seeded, n=5, spread 0.00 -- still can, and is now the only C++ case with a defensible number.
